notes.title: Striden | Hotfix Update & Upcoming Content News
notes.content: [h3][b]Hello Rebels![/b][/h3][p]We’re finally ready to roll out our delayed hotfix patch! Just to be clear: we’ve been working on two updates at the same time. The hotfix goes live today, and at the end of September we’ll be releasing our very first [b]content update patch[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]Let’s start by talking about that upcoming content update. Over the past two weeks, we’ve begun development on a brand-new game mode with the working title [b]Kontroll[/b]. It’s heavily inspired by Domination/Conquest, but with a unique Striden twist.[/p][p][/p][p]Our goal with Kontroll is to create a mode that’s easy to jump into for new players: pick a soldier class, choose your weapon loadout, and get straight into the action. Expect fast-paced matches with quick respawns, set in a section of our brand-new map [b]Nuke 08[/b], which takes place in Stockholm, Sweden. Nuke 08 is being built specifically with Kontroll in mind, based on community feedback. Matches will be [b]5v5 (10 players total)[/b], and just like in Transmit, you’ll still progress through ranks and unlock weapons. We’ll share more details in future updates![/p][p]On top of that, we’re also adding a brand-new [b]Transmit map[/b] called [b]Souppat[/b]—a reimagining of our co-op map [i]Berget[/i], redesigned to fit perfectly into Transmit.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]This hotfix patch we release today will include:[/h3][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Easy Anti-Cheat[/b] fully integrated into the game[/p][/*][*][p][b]New backend monitoring system[/b] – lets us see what’s happening on the servers without logging into the game, making it easier to act against disruptive users and gather data for balancing[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mute function[/b] in the scoreboard for VOIP/Proximity chat + soldier voice lines[/p][/*][*][p][b]Bug fixes[/b] for explosive weapons dealing damage through walls[/p][/*][*][p][b]Toggle sprint function[/b] added[/p][/*][*][p][b]Toggle crouch function[/b] added[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rank corrections[/b] – We are working on an overhaul of the progression system to fix lost ranks. We can now restore lost or bugged ranks retroactively. If you have lost your rank, send us a DM in our Discord. [/p][/*][*][p][b]DLSS bug.[/b] Fixed excessive Log Spamming caused by DLSS incorrectly trying to enable itself[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Next up, we’re gearing up for the Steam event at the end of September! That’s when we’ll restart our marketing push, pack the servers, and bring Striden roaring back to life![/p][p][/p][h2][i][b]Don´t miss out our [u]Let´s play Striden[/u] event every Saturday 7:00PM CET[/b][/i][/h2][p][/p][h3]Don’t forget to join our  [url="https://discord.com/invite/Wyjcw5Qu6B" style="button"] Discord[/url]  for behind-the-scenes content, direct chats with the devs, a place to share your feedback, and to team up with fellow Rebels to play Striden![/h3]

notes.title: IS STRIDEN DEAD?!
notes.content:
[h2][b]Here we are, one month after Early Access.[/b]
[/h2][p]“[b]How does it feel?[/b]” that’s probably what a sports reporter would ask us right now.[/p][p]To be completely honest with you: it didn’t exactly go as we had hoped.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/9a6414122543c1c86bb9b5a665d66a40769d21bb.png"][/img][/p][p]Our plan was to make a bigger PR push with traditional media & social media right at launch day, one month ago.[/p][p]That part actually went well, bigger gaming outlets and websites wrote about [i]Striden[/i], and we had good traction on social media and in the game itself.[/p][p]The next step was to ramp things up over the weekend with bigger YouTubers and streamers who would test the game, spread the word, and bring in more players beyond those who already knew about [i]Striden[/i]. Everything was prepared and ready to go.[/p][p][/p][p]But then we hit a serious problem. Someone or several people apparently decided it was a very bad idea for [i]Striden[/i] to launch, and started sabotaging our servers. On top of that, we discovered internal data breaches in the studio.[/p][p]The breaking point came when streamer [b]Lirik[/b] was about to test [i]Striden[/i] live on Twitch only for the griefer to find the server he was on and make the game unplayable for him. Around the same time, we also saw unauthorized access to our GitHub, where we manage all files and builds for the game.[/p][p][/p][p]At that point, we had to pull the emergency brake. We couldn’t justify putting money into marketing. Instead, we urgently had to strengthen our anti-cheat, investigate who was behind this, and protect the project.[/p][p][/p][p]This also took a toll on the team. Some of us burned out after working day and night for a long time to deliver a solid build for Early Access. A few team members needed to take well-earned time off to recharge and spend time with family. We’re human, after all.[/p][p][/p][p]That said, development didn’t stop during July and August. We put a lot of resources into improving security both internally and for the game. The sabotage investigation has been ongoing, and we’ve made real progress pieces of the puzzle are falling into place.[/p][p]Now, we’re starting to feel [b]ready[/b] for a new push to bring the servers back to life. More on that later.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What have we actually worked on in July and August?[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]Easy Anti-Cheat[/b] fully integrated into the game[/p][/*][*][p][b]New backend monitoring system[/b] – lets us see what’s happening on the servers without logging into the game, making it easier to act against disruptive users and gather data for balancing[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mute function[/b] in the scoreboard for VOIP/Proximity chat + soldier voice lines[/p][/*][*][p][b]New file management solution[/b] in the studio, plus additional security measures[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sabotage investigation[/b] – ongoing, with authorities now involved[/p][/*][*][p][b]Bug fixes[/b] for explosive weapons dealing damage through walls[/p][/*][*][p][b]Toggle sprint function[/b] added[/p][/*][*][p][b]Toggle crouch function[/b] added[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rank corrections[/b] – we can now restore lost or bugged ranks retroactively[/p][/*][/list][p]We’re aiming to release this as a [b]hotfix this coming week[/b], if all tests go well.[/p][p]We know this hotfix alone won’t bring back player numbers but it’s an important step before our next big push.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What’s next for Striden?[/b][/h3][p]We are now back in full strength again.[/p][p]At the [b]end of September[/b], we’ll release our first [b]content update[/b], aligned with the [b][u]Steam Autumn Sale[/u][/b]. Here, we’ll focus on offering a compelling price point to bring more players back. A new map for the [i]Transmit[/i] game mode will be included, along with other changes based on your feedback.[/p][p]Beyond that, we’re sticking to our roadmap. Current projects in production include:[/p][list][*][p]Matchmaking system[/p][/*][*][p]Friend lobby system[/p][/*][*][p]A [b]new game mode[/b] that’s simpler, easier to learn, and fun without needing 20 players[/p][/*][*][p]A new map to go with the new mode[/p][/*][*][p]More bug fixes[/p][/*][*][p]Ongoing content updates based on community feedback[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]So, is Striden dead?[/b][/h3][p]No. We know the player numbers are low right now, and we’re just as frustrated about it as you are. But the game is not dead. We have secured funding for production all the way to full launch.[/p][p]I do want to point out, however, that we are an extremely small studio with a very limited budget for a project like this.[/p][p]Some of us have been working on this for over 5 years, so we’re not about to give up anytime soon. But without you, it will be difficult![/p][p]Your early support in buying [i]Striden[/i] during Early Access has been a huge help in financing servers and future marketing efforts. With that said, we’re looking forward working hard to make [i]Striden[/i] better than ever.[/p][p]A huge thank you to everyone who believes in [i]Striden[/i]. If you’re eager to play, join our Discord you’ll definitely find others ready to squad up. And if you haven’t yet, you can try our [b]Co-op prototype[/b], which already includes nearly all the core elements of the PvP mode.[/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.com/invite/Wyjcw5Qu6B" buttoncolor="#1b9d2a"]JOIN OUR DISCORD[/url][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Early Access | First weekend
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Rebels![/h1][p][/p][p][b]First of all, thank you for an amazing first weekend![/b]
Reaching Early Access is a huge milestone for us, and we’re incredibly happy to see so much interest in our new take on the first-person shooter genre. This is just the beginning, a journey we’re excited to take together with our community as we build the next great FPS.[/p][p][/p][p]We've seen many new players join STRIDEN, and we’re also thrilled to welcome back those of you who participated in our earlier playtests. [/p][p]We hadn’t planned for or expected the game to explode with so many new players in the first few days. But from our perspective, everything is going according to plan, slowly but surely building a dedicated player base that believes in the game and wants to help shape it in the right direction.[/p][p][/p][p]As a brand-new IP developed by a small indie team, our community means everything to us. Most of our player base is currently in Europe, so you’ll see peak activity during the afternoon and evening CET.[/p][p]Over time, as word spreads, we hope to see more players from around the world join the fight. For now, we’re incredibly grateful to everyone who’s already investing their time in STRIDEN. Thank you for your support.[/p][p][/p][h1]Cheaters[/h1][p]Unfortunately, we’re currently dealing with a serious issue: a cheater/hacker who seems intent on sabotaging the game. We take this very seriously. Not only has the game itself been targeted, but our studio, 5 Fortress, has also been hacked, impacting our internal servers, including those handling project files and project management. Our teams at 5 Fortress and Yahaha Games are working around the clock to respond to this attack.[/p][p]While we can’t share all the details, please know we are actively addressing the situation.[/p][p]This week, we’re prioritizing a hotfix to address the cheating issue and improve the game's security.[/p][p]We also gonna do some smaller tweaks and fixes for the gameplay / game.[/p][p]Thank you for your patience and understanding as we work through this.[/p][p][/p][p]Aside from this, we continue to read every piece of feedback and bug report we receive. Your input is invaluable in helping us improve and evolve STRIDEN.[/p][p][/p][h1]Roadmap[/h1][p]Last week was hectic, so apologies for the rough version of the roadmap we initially shared. Here's an updated version with some of the issues you pointed out fixed. We're also working on a cleaner, more readable version that we plan to release in the coming weeks. Thanks for your patience and feedback![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/03e7f3b7bc550f47f062d86e01bdadf44fc6e2fa.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The best way to tell what do you think about the game and give us feedback are to join our [url="https://discord.com/invite/Wyjcw5Qu6B"]Discord Community[/url][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Only one week left until Open Beta
notes.content: [h2]Hello Rebels! [/h2][p][/p][p][b]So, what have we been up to this past week?[/b] Our main focus has been working on our Open Beta build, which will go live on June 27th. As usual, we’ve been tweaking, balancing, and optimizing the game. But we’ve also added some new content![/p][p]We’ve continued working on [b]Powerspikes[/b] (Animals), and one of the new features is that we’ve recorded motion capture animations. So now, when you channel into your animal, a third-person “dance” animation will play, letting others see that you’re about to become, for example, a Bear. Speaking of Bears… you can now [u][b]ride[/b][/u] them! Yes, as a soldier, you can ride your teammate’s Bear.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="peV6oeHASvw;full"][/previewyoutube][p]One of our main tasks this week has been to create a smoother experience with less flickering when you see a player getting attached to an enemy eagle hook or riding a bear. We feel that it’s finally starting to look good![/p][p][/p][p][b]Construction Items[/b][/p][p]We’ve now added 3D widget icons for every interactive construction item you can build in your Stronghold. This makes it easier for teammates to see where everything is in the base.[/p][p]We’ve also made the Medic’s construction item the Class Wardrobe fully functional. Now you don’t need to respawn to change class. Just interact with the wardrobe and switch classes instantly. During our last internal playtest, we noticed that being able to change class in your base encourages players to stay a bit longer and build everything up properly.[/p][previewyoutube="daNE8CD5L28;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p] [b]Menus and Server Browser[/b][/p][p]This week, we started creating mock-ups for how the menus will look in the game. I think the progress already looks really good![/p][p][/p][p]( Work in Progress )[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/d44054781c22c32d7ccfb3ff2333ddd32f1e4fa7.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/759a09b05f7093add7a7c21ac92be04965036f94.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/de090d1d870fd3df8d98d928cbd41529a5769342.png"][/img][/p][p]Yes, and as is now tradition leading up to Early Access, we’ll keep bringing you along with us into our studio where we work every day. Or maybe we should start calling it our madhouse instead? We’re all starting to go a bit crazy now that Open Beta is so close![/p][previewyoutube="3ZKm_Ibi-HA;full"][/previewyoutube][p]See you next weekend in [b]STRIDEN[/b]![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Open Beta around the corner & Development update
notes.content: [h2]Hello Rebels! [/h2][p][/p][p][b]Time for our grand finale playtest session of STRIDEN before the Early Access launch! On June 27th, we’re opening up our playtest app to the public for one final free playtest weekend. To join, make sure to sign up for the playtest on our Steam page.[/b][/p][p][b]If you’ve played before, just sit back and relax, you’ll automatically get access when the beta starts.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]So, what have we been up to this past week?[/b][/p][p]We’ve been fully focused on tracking down bugs, fixing performance issues, and preparing our back-end systems.[/p][p]Every week, we run at least one internal test, and we’ve also held two stress test sessions with full servers playing STRIDEN for about three hours each to make sure everything works as it should.[/p][p]Our talented, tight-knit team has been hard at work developing fresh new content and replacing placeholder assets.[/p][p][/p][p]Our team of interns has made fantastic progress on our new urban map, [b]Nuke 08[/b].[/p][p][b]Nuke 08[/b] is set in Sweden’s capital, Stockholm, where a tactical nuke has destroyed large parts of the city. This setting brings a fresh twist to the game and stands out from our other maps — with a mix of tight close-quarters combat areas and wide open streets with varied elevation.[/p][p]This new map won’t be included in the Open Beta, but we’re aiming to have a playable version ready by late summer 2025.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/63b99d3c5f8fa55eef7cb9ad4db1b41dca61486a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/720b31b6477c704578971f28f3e872efdf824c47.png"][/img][/p][h2]Progress with our Powerspikes[/h2][p]The biggest update is that we’ve added a new system to how Powerspikes work. Now, you have to choose which Powerspike (animal) you want to play [b]before[/b] each match — and you’ll be locked to that animal for the entire match. You make your choice in the match lobby before deploying onto the battlefield.[/p][p]This means your team will need to think more strategically about which Powerspikes fit the map and your overall tactics. Powerspikes still charge up based on your individual player score, and when you activate them, you must place them carefully on the map [b]no more Moose Tanks spawning inside Strongholds![/b] It also now takes time to channel into your chosen animal, so you can’t instantly spawn a Powerspike anymore. Enemies can attack you while you’re channeling, so pick your moment and location wisely.[/p][p]We’ve also removed the timer for how long you can stay in your Powerspike. Now, you can cancel it at any time. Plus, you can now spot enemy Powerspikes to alert your teammates.[/p][p]With these changes, Powerspike balance has improved significantly not every player can just summon a bear or a Moose Tank anymore.[/p][p][/p][p]Our beloved [b]Moose Tank[/b] has received a lot of love too. We’ve reworked its driving and movement to make it feel less clunky. Enemies can now destroy the Moose itself, which disables the cannon turret — so if you’re facing one, aim for the Moose! Think of it like tracking a tank in other games.[/p][p][/p][p]The [b]Radioactive Bear[/b] has also been polished for smoother movement. The biggest new feature is that teammates can now [b]ride[/b] a friendly bear! Just approach it, hold the interact button, and voilà, you’re basically Rambo on a Scandinavian bear.[/p][p][/p][p]For the [b]Eagle Hook[/b], we’ve continued improving the flight controls. This Powerspike is quickly becoming a STRIDEN favorite, it opens up a whole new dimension for transporting teammates or trolling enemies by grabbing them and dropping them from the sky.[/p][p][/p][p]The [b]Bomber Eagle[/b] is both amazing and terrifying, depending on which side you’re on. Having a flying bomb plane in STRIDEN is perfect for clearing out an Air Supply zone or blasting a pesky sniper hiding on a hill.[/p][p]But once we added birds to the game, we realized something was missing. A counter to hunt them down. So, naturally, we made a fighter jet… well, a [b]Fighter Eagle[/b]! This bad boy comes equipped with a light machine gun (MG-42) and two air-to-ground missiles. So keep an eye on the skies during the next playtest![/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="ebcui1l8zMk;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]Personality for the Class Soldiers[/h2][p]All of our soldier voices have now been replaced with real voice actors — a huge milestone for us, finally replacing all the placeholder lines in the game. Some lines have already become iconic, so we made sure to keep a few classics while adding plenty of new ones. With real voice talent, we were able to get much more creative and bring our soldiers to life.[/p][p]We’ve also programmed soldiers to react more naturally to what’s happening around them. For example, they now shout warnings about incoming grenades, scream or curse when suppressed, and react vocally when they take damage. These changes have made a big difference to the game’s immersion — now it really feels like you’re in the middle of a chaotic, intense battle.[/p][p]More shouts, more personality, and even more epic moments for everyone![/p][previewyoutube="_ejnnonvHb4;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]Suppression & New Death Camera[/h2][p]As I mentioned when talking about the new soldier voices, we’ve now added a [b]suppression system[/b] to the game. Before you tear your hair out, don’t worry! It’s very subtle, but it makes the combat feel more intense and realistic, adding to the immersion when bullets whip past your head.[/p][p]We’re also planning to fine-tune it so that different weapons cause different levels of suppression. For example, light machine guns will create more suppression than a submachine gun.[/p][previewyoutube="dABaJyXxzpQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p]So, if you get suppressed, take a few bullets, and get killed you’ll now see it all through our improved death camera. Previously, we had a first-person death sequence, but in about 80% of cases, you’d just see your body flying away like a happy dolphin in the ocean. It looked odd, and we also got feedback that the kill cam lingered too long on the enemy who killed you.[/p][p]Now, your view follows the head of your soldier as they fall, making the sequence feel much more grounded and realistic. We’ve also added new camera effects to enhance the impact. Plus, the time spent showing the enemy who killed you has been shortened for a smoother experience.[/p][p][/p][h2]Construction System — Almost Finished[/h2][p]A big part of the game is our [b]construction system[/b], which isn’t just for base defense and team resources it also plays a key strategic role out on the battlefield. We’ve now polished the repair system, including how the [b]Sentry Gun[/b] works. Enemies can destroy a Sentry Gun, but not completely the owning team can repair it and bring it back into action.[/p][p]We’ve also renamed our [b]Vending Machine[/b] to [b]Loot Storage[/b] to make its purpose clearer: it’s for storing loot. A new feature is that Loot Storage now generates new consumables over time. So, when you respawn at your base ([b]Stronghold[/b]), you can grab a can of beans or other supplies before heading back into the fight.[/p][p]If you raid an enemy Stronghold and destroy their construction items, you’ll be rewarded with blueprints. And if you destroy an item that stores loot like a weapon station all the stored items will be dropped on the ground.[/p][p]So make sure your base defenses are solid![/p][p][/p][h2]Respawn System[/h2][p]We’re currently working on a [b]spawn protection system[/b] to reduce spawn killing, with a main focus on protecting Strongholds (bases). This has been a common piece of feedback for a long time players getting killed by base campers and we hope this update will help solve that issue.[/p][p]We’ve also added a change so that you always respawn with a full clip/magazine after being killed. Additionally, we’re working on a system where, if you join a match already in progress, you’ll spawn with a basic submachine gun to get you into the action right away.[/p][p][/p][h2]Radioactivity — Less Deadly[/h2][p]After replacing our placeholder radioactive fog with our epic dynamic weather system, we realized we wanted players to engage in more battles during radioactive storms. So, we’ve tweaked how much radiation drains your gas mask filter and how much damage it deals. Now, your filter lasts longer, giving you more time to fight in radioactive zones.[/p][p][/p][h2]Audio[/h2][p]We’re still working on sound mixing to make sure we don’t blow out your eardrums during intense firefights. With so many sounds playing at once and a lot happening on-screen, getting the balance right is a big challenge, especially since we don’t have a dedicated audio engineer in the studio. But we’re doing our best to deliver a great audio experience for Early Access, with proper reverb zones and realistic sound behavior at different distances.[/p][p][/p][h2]UI/UX[/h2][p]We’ve started production on new menus to make navigating the settings and other screens much easier. Up until now, we’ve been using very basic placeholders, but what the team is working on now looks really promising.[/p][p][/p][h2]Bugs and Performance[/h2][p]Of course, we’ve also been busy fixing bugs and improving performance over the past week. We spend a lot of time on this to ensure a smoother experience for everyone. One of the biggest fixes was resolving screen tearing and flickering, this was a nightmare to track down, but switching to a different anti-aliasing method finally solved it.[/p][p]We’ve also made server performance more stable, especially on our 60 Hz servers.[/p][p][/p][h2]Less Than a Month to Early Access Launch![/h2][p]We’re working around the clock to deliver an amazing first version of STRIDEN, and we couldn’t be more excited to share it with players around the world. As mentioned in earlier blog posts, this is just the beginning of our journey. Together with you, our community, we’ll shape a fast-paced, fun, and action-packed looter shooter.[/p][p]We’re committed to listening to your feedback not only for fine-tuning gameplay but also for shaping future content. Your voice will truly have an impact on the development of STRIDEN.[/p][p][b]Early Access will be priced at $24.99[/b], with a special 20% launch-week discount to thank our early supporters. This pricing ensures we can maintain servers and continue developing the game without relying on crowdfunding. When you buy STRIDEN, you’re directly supporting our team and the game’s future.[/p][p]We’re also planning cosmetic DLC soldier skins, weapon skins, and more that will be purely optional and won’t affect gameplay. No pay-to-win mechanics or map-based DLCs that split the player base.[/p][p][/p][p]Starting now, we’ll post weekly updates here on Steam leading up to launch, plus exclusive behind-the-scenes footage from our studio where 80% of the team is hard at work bringing STRIDEN to life.[/p][p]Get ready STRIDEN’s Early Access is just around the corner![/p][previewyoutube="dNG0FZAGq3c;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Join our [url="https://discord.gg/Wyjcw5Qu6B"]Discord[/url] to join our community and say hey to the devs![/p][p][b]Take care and see you at the Open Beta June 27th.[/b][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Early Access Release Date and Dev Updates
notes.content:
[b][u]Hello Rebels![/u][/b]

Time for a fresh update on what's happening with [b]STRIDEN[/b] and the progress we’ve made!

With the Open Beta still fresh in our minds, we've learned a lot. First off, implementing a new network code can introduce new challenges but ultimately, it boosts performance. So, what caused our network issues?

We’ve made several updates to hit registration to create a more consistent and satisfying gunplay experience. We’ve also reworked the progression system and increased server tickrates. While these changes were necessary, they did affect server reliability and had a negative impact on proximity chat and servers. But after a lot of hard work, we’re now in a [u]much better[/u] place with nearly everything back on track.

To ensure stability, we’ve partnered with Nortify, a QA company that’s stress-testing our game with long sessions and full servers. We’re determined to make the next playtest a rock-solid experience for all of you.

We also fixed one of our most frustrating bugs "The Terminator Bug" which caused some players to become immortal. A nasty glitch that made it look like people were cheating. [u]Not anymore[/u].

While analyzing kill and death events, we also squashed the annoying kill trade bug. No more mysterious simultaneous kills during hectic firefights!

Gunplay now feels tighter and more responsive. We’ve added first-person tracers to better visualize spread and bloom, and improved third-person tracers so you can clearly see where enemies are firing from.

[h2]Now, for the big news:[/h2]

[b]STRIDEN is launching into Early Access on July 11![/b]
This is a huge milestone for us. After more than three years of development (and over 600 hours of internal playtesting on my part alone), we’re finally ready to open the gates.

[h2]So what does Early Access mean for STRIDEN?[/h2]

It’s the beginning of our journey with you—the community. We’re releasing a solid first version of the game, and we’ll keep building from here, actively listening to your feedback. A roadmap is on the way, outlining our plans through to full release about a year from now.

Your voice will help shape the game. You’ll be able to vote on things like the next map or weapon, beyond what’s already planned. We want to develop STRIDEN with the community—not just for it.

[h2]About us:[/h2]
5-Fortress is a small indie studio based in northern Sweden. At our largest, we’ve been 8 developers; for the past 8 months, it’s been just 3 of us, supported by talented interns from local game development programs. Recently, we’ve partnered with Yahaha Games, which is allowing us to scale up again. They’re also helping us with backend infrastructure for launch—ensuring we deliver on our promises.

Our goal: a high-quality indie FPS looter-shooter that stands out from the AAA crowd. No pay-to-win. No paid battle passes. A fresh take on familiar mechanics with a tight, fun gameloop—and always developed in conversation with you, the community.

[h2]Here’s a sneak peek of what we’ve been working on lately:[/h2]

☢️ [b]New Radioactive Fog/Storm[/b]
The old green fog was… fine. But now, the radioactive storm brings dynamic weather that affects visibility, atmosphere, and the soundscape of the entire map. Way more immersive—and way more intense.

[previewyoutube=fTuJRdPIOgg;full][/previewyoutube]


🧰 [b]New Lobby System – Customize Your Class[/b]
You’ll now be able to tailor your class to your playstyle—pick your construction items, outfits (coming soon!), and most importantly, your Powerspike. Only one Powerspike per match, making for deeper team strategy. Plus, this system sets the stage for adding more content in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/db23891e28f02a3d67fe16b8b45d2a5572bf8650.png[/img]

🗺️ [b]New Tactical Map – Plan to Win[/b]
A redesigned map interface makes it easier to navigate, issue commands, and coordinate with your team. Zoom in and out, mark objectives, and take control of the match flow like never before.


🦅 [b]Polished Powerspikes[/b]
We’ll have 5 Powerspikes available in Early Access. The newest? Birds. Yes, really.
“Eagle Hook” can fly teammates across the map—or drop enemies from altitude.
“Bomb Eagle”? Just what it sounds like.
We're also revisiting old favorites like the Bear and Moose, improving movement and fixing spawn logic (no more Moose Tanks inside Strongholds).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/03e1c316337d7a294d196a2b887e47bc3b78f778.png[/img]


🌆 [b]New Map – Urban Combat[/b]
Our amazing interns are working on something epic: a nuked town full of massive ruined buildings and hidden military bunkers. Think brutal, intense, and full of tactical opportunities.

🎶 [b]Our own soundtrack[/b]
We are removing all placeholder music and going full scale on a own STRIDEN soundtrack.

There’s even [b]more[/b] exciting content coming soon. We’re going all in on this and hope you’ll enjoy everything we’re building.

[b]We’re planning one last Open Playtest before the Early Access launch on July 11—stay tuned![/b]

Please help us spread the word—tell your friends, tell your rivals—and make sure to Wishlist STRIDEN and follow us on Steam. Don’t forget to join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/Wyjcw5Qu6B]Discord[/url] for weekly updates and to share your feedback directly.

Take care,
/Johan

notes.title: OPEN BETA IS LIVE!
notes.content:
Hello!

After participating in Steam Next Fest and running our own playtest over the holiday season, we have carefully listened to player feedback. We've made significant changes to the game to show that this time, we truly care!

Now, we’re ready to enter Open Beta and welcome more players to sink their teeth into STRIDEN. At 5-Fortress, our goal is to create a first-person shooter where the community’s voice is heard from day one. We want to take a step back to how FPS games used to be-avoiding the modern trend where games spiral into chaos with outrageous skins, making them look like a messy bachelor party after just a few months.

When many new systems and features are added, bugs are inevitable. That’s one of the reasons we conduct open playtests—to stress-test our game and gather data to refine and polish everything.

Over the past few weeks, we’ve been working hard to resolve network-related issues. Most of these were on the server side, particularly when using our hosting system for larger events. While we’ve fixed most of the problems and are ready for testing, there’s still some work left to do. That’s why we’re holding another Open Beta test this coming weekend. So have that in mind this weekend.

We’re getting closer to Early Access, and these playtests are crucial in shaping the game’s future.

[h1]Weapons & Gunplay Changes[/h1]

All firing sound effects have been reworked, including the rules for sound distance. It is now easier to determine how far away an enemy is when they fire. We have used real recordings of various weapon types, captured with microphones placed at different distances, making the experience more authentic and immersive. Additionally, all foley sounds have been redone. We hope this change will satisfy those who gave us feedback that the weapons needed more impact.

We have also started developing a weapon progression system, where you need to progress with a weapon to unlock new variants. This system is still a work in progress and [u]will not be included in the Open Beta[/u] due to bugs. However, our weapon skin progression system will be available in the Beta. While still under development, you will be able to unlock weapon skins during this test.

[u][b]Assault Rifle Adjustments[/b][/u]

Assault rifles have been overhauled, with increased damage per bullet and greater heat spread when firing from the hip. Recoil patterns have also been adjusted. Assault rifles are now most effective at mid-range when aiming down sights. Speaking of aiming, ADS (aim down sights) speed has been reduced across all assault rifles to improve the balance, making submachine guns more effective at close range. Additionally, the cost to purchase an assault rifle has been increased from 10 to 12 common weapon parts. You can now also switch to single-fire mode on assault rifles by pressing [b]V[/b] on the keyboard.

[u]Assault Rifles Changelog:[/u]

¤ AK-4 : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.
¤ M16 : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread + 3 new variants.
¤ AK47: Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.
¤ FN-FAL : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread, reduced fire rate + 2 new variants.

[u][b]Submachine Guns: A Balancing Challenge[/b][/u]

Balancing weapons in a shooter game is always a challenge. Buffing one weapon can make another feel weaker. So, what have we done to make submachine guns more viable in STRIDEN? Many players have given us feedback that SMGs feel underpowered—most players opt for an assault rifle as soon as they have enough weapon parts.
To address this, we've made several key changes. Submachine guns now deal slightly higher damage, with increased damage falloff. However, the biggest improvements come in handling: faster aim-down-sight (ADS) speed and reduced heat spread when firing from the hip. Additionally, SMGs offer significantly better mobility compared to assault rifles.
With these changes, submachine guns are now the go-to choice for close-quarters combat.

[u]Submachine gun Changelog:[/u]

¤ Sten Gun MK II : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread + 2 new variants.
¤ Swedish K : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread + 2 variants now have a higher rate of fire.
¤ KP-31 : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.
¤ AKS 47u : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread + 1 new variant.

We've been working on tweaking light machine guns (LMGs) to put them in a more balanced position. They are now slightly harder to control, but their damage has been increased. Mobility is more restricted, making them feel heavier, but they are the perfect weapon for suppressing enemies or spraying down an opposing team from mid-range. With higher firepower than assault rifles, LMGs now stand out as a powerful choice for sustained fire.

[u]LMG Changelog:[/u]

¤ L 26 :  Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.
¤ VM 76 : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.
¤ M60 : Adjusted recoil pattern and heat spread.

We found that rifles in STRIDEN are already in a good place, so we haven't made any major changes to them.

[u]Rifle Changelog:[/u]

¤ SVT 40: Added 2 new variants.
¤ Mosin Nagant 9130: Added 2 new variants.

[h1]Explosives: Fixes & Balancing[/h1]

Explosives have been one of the most broken weapon systems in the game. Previously, you could throw a grenade outside a building and still damage enemies inside through the walls.

Before you hate us, this was due to a wall-bang system we had implemented—but it was so unstable that we had to temporarily remove it.

Now, that system has been fully reworked and will be included in the Beta. Different materials will now filter explosive damage—for example, a thin hollow wooden wall will let more damage through, while a solid metal wall will completely block it. The level of penetration will also depend on the type of explosive used. This system is still being tested and fine-tuned, but it will be part of the Beta.
We’ve also added armor-piercing explosives. These will be especially effective against construction items and power spikes with thicker armor or stronger materials.

[h2]New Breaching Mechanics & Resupply Changes[/h2]

Breach charges have been introduced, allowing for quick door breaches. This item is exclusive to the Assault class as part of their construction tools.


Explosive resupply has been reworked. Previously, Support players could spam grenade launchers and instantly refill ammo using an ammo box. This has now changed. To resupply explosives, an Assault player must construct an Explosive Stash crate inside a Stronghold. This ensures a more balanced use of explosives in the game.

[u]Explosives Changelog:[/u]

¤ F1 Soviet Grenade: Increased damage radius and overall damage. Low penetration.
¤ M79 Grenade Launcher: Increased damage, but with a smaller damage radius. Medium penetration.
¤ GRK-48 (Fragmentation): Increased damage with a medium radius. Medium penetration.
¤ GRK-48 (Armor-Piercing): Small damage radius but high penetration.
¤ Dynamite Stick: Increased throwing velocity, higher damage and radius. Low penetration.


[h1]Construction system[/h1]
We’ve completely rewritten the construction mechanics, allowing enemy players to destroy opposing team structures. The new health and armor system now means different weapons deal varying amounts of damage to constructions. Players will need to repair windows and doors if enemies breach their base. Additionally, we’ve addressed exploits that allowed players to block all entry points to their base. On top of this, we’ve expanded the construction system with more items available to all soldier classes. We’re incredibly excited to hear player feedback on this!

[u][b]Soldier class construction items:[/b][/u]

[b]Assault:[/b]

                ¤ Explosive Stash - Refill explosive ammo
                ¤ Sentrygun - Guards your Stronghold from intruders

[b]Engineer: [/b]

                ¤ Sandbag wall - Barricade wall that you can construct outside
                ¤ Barricade wall - Barricade wall that you can construct in your Stronghold

[b]Medic:[/b]

[b]Support:[/b]

               ¤ Trophy system - Defend a small radius from explosives

[b]Spotter:[/b]

                  landscape. You can switch camouflage color by interacting with it.
               ¤ Alert Rocket - Tripwire that's triggered by enemies. Spotting all enemies close to the impact 
               ¤ Landmine - Personal mine that hides in the landscape. Perfect trap for intruders


[h1]Improved Mid-Game Joining[/h1]

Players joining a match mid-game will no longer be thrown straight into the action. Instead, you’ll now be able to choose your team and spawn location. We’ve also fixed the frustrating bug from our holiday playtest, where players joining a co-op match mid-game would get stuck on a black screen.

[h1]A Major Game-Changer[/h1]

The Electron Tube Transport Mechanic: Previously, players could carry the Electron Tube while still using their weapons. Now, when transporting an Electron Tube to your base, you must physically hold it in your hands. This forces teams to work together more strategically and protect their transporters.


[b]We have a lot more in the pipeline,[/b] including systems that didn’t make it into the Open Beta. One of them is our vaulting and mantling system, which still needs some refinement before it’s ready for testing. We will publish a roadmap as we get closer to Early Access.

notes.title: Open Beta 28th March
notes.content:
[u][b]Hello rebel fighters! [/b][/u]

So, we’ve been really busy since our last holiday playtest. We’ve gathered all your feedback from the last session and put in a ton of work to address the things you didn’t like. As we’ve mentioned earlier, your feedback is key to making the game even better, and our goal is to create a first-person shooter together with the player base.

So what have we been up to lately? 

[u][b]Reworked construction system[/b][/u]

Construction in Striden is a major feature that changes the battlefield dynamics and enhances defense. It’s also key to securing your loadout for a match, so it’s important to us that it works well with the gameplay.

We have reworked the system and implemented damage rules and armor for each construction type. For example, you can now destroy any enemy construction. Blow up barricades with your grenade launcher or destroy enemy weapon stations to steal all their weapon parts.

Destruction introduces a new feature to Striden—repair. Yes, you now need your construction tool to fix breached doors and windows.

We have also reviewed where players can build inside their Stronghold. This was a major issue in the last playtest. Many players were constructing Vending Machines to block doors, leaving enemies with no way to destroy or remove them. This is no longer possible.

New motion capture animations have been created for the Vending Machine and Weapon Station, adding more life to these assets.

New hit markers and impact sounds have been added to provide better player feedback. This helps you know if your weapon is dealing damage to construction items.

Now, every soldier class has three unique construction items to build.

[b]Assault [/b]

- Breach Charge : You can use them on doors and windows to fast breach into a area / Stronghold
- Explosive Stash : Only way to rearm your explosives.
- Sentry gun: Guards your Stronghold from enemies.

[b]Engineer[/b]

- Barricade Wall: Defends your team from explosives and gunfire
- Barricade Windowed: Gives great covers and also a windows to shoot from.
- Sandbag Wall: Give you and your team cover outside, for example near a Air Supply.

[b]Support[/b]

- Ammo Crate : Resupply your team with ammo inside your Stronghold
- Vending Machine: Store consumable loot for your team. 
- Trophy System: Destroy incoming explosives projectiles in air.

[b]Medic[/b]

- Healing Station: Eat some warm soup inside your Stronghold and gain HP
- Class Wardrobe: Change soldier class without killing yourself.
- Unknown

[b]Spotter[/b]

- Alert Rocket: A tripwire trap connected to a firework rocket. When it's triggers it will spot all enemies close to the zone it was triggered from.
- Bouncing Betty Mine: Personal landmine
- Camo Hut: Build a small camo tent outside. Switch between 3 camo presets. Woods/Urban/Winter. You can´t be spotted by a enemies if you are inside a camo hut. 

We have polish UX/UI for construction items to. 

[u][b]Join mid-game / Updated lobby system.[/b][/u]

Now you can join an ongoing match and choose which team you want to play on. This is something players have been asking for a while, so we’re really happy to finally have this feature in the game.

We have also started working on finishing the lobby system, but it won’t be ready in time for the Open Beta.

[u][b]Player traversing & vault/mantle system[/b][/u]

We are at the movement working on our vault / mantle system for the game. We really hope that we can get a working version in place for the Open Beta. 

[u][b]Electron Tube game changer[/b][/u]

A big change to the game is that when you pick up an electron tube from an air supply, you now unequip your weapon and hold the electron tube physically. To drop the tube, you need to switch to your weapon or construction tool.

This change makes it more challenging to transport electron tubes to your Stronghold. Now, you’ll need assistance from teammates to defend you.

We have conducted internal tests of this feature, and players really like the change.

[u][b]Weapon Overhaul[/b][/u]

All weapons have been reworked. I’ll go into more detail about these changes later, but I can hint that the TTK is slightly faster and the different weapon classes now make more sense.

A new hitmarker UI has also been added—now you’ll really feel the feedback when landing a headshot!

[u][b]Weapon Skins & Progression[/b][/u]

Weapon skins are now in the game! Unlock skins by using your weapon, and now you also need to unlock different weapon upgrades. Our progression system is coming along well!


[u][b]All weapon sounds are reworked[/b][/u]

More dynamics and punch! Yes, we’ve received feedback that the weapons in Striden lacked impact in their sound design. So now, every weapon has been given new or remastered sounds.

This has been a huge amount of work, but the weapon sounds are now much more dynamic and powerful. We’ve also redone all weapon foley sounds, such as reload sounds.

[u][b]Sound fixes and mastering[/b][/u]

We have been looking over the full soundscape in Striden, everything from footsteps to sound mixes. 
Added sound features like audio ducking and max amount of played sounds at the same time for performance. 

[u][b]VOIP/Proximity chat[/b][/u]

Striden had a nasty bug in the last playtest—if you kept talking in VOIP when the server switched maps, it would crash for everyone.

We’ve now fixed that bug and also reworked the VOIP system a bit. Your teammates now have a walkie-talkie filter effect on their voices, and we’ve added a compressor/limiter to prevent loud players from making you deaf.


[u][b]New Striden logotype and cover-art[/b][/u]

We are closing into Early Access and internally we call this STRIDEN 2.0. We going from less prototyping content and removing placeholders. One of them are our logotype and cover art. Hope you like our new branding of the game.

[u][b]Bug fixes and surprises[/b][/u]

We have fixed a lot of bugs from the last playtest. We will share a full patch notes list of all the changes when we launch the Open Beta.

But one of the biggest issues has been fixed: the Full-Screen Glitch Bug and the Black Screen Bug in CO-OP.

We still want to give you guys some surprises to the Open Beta. So more to come end of this month.

Open Beta Starts: 

28th March and ends 30th March.

Want to have more frequently updates join our Discord for daily updates.

notes.title: CHRISTMAS PLAYTEST AROUND THE CORNER!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello everyone and Merry Christmas!

We want to give something special as a gift from us at 5-fortress to celebrate Christmas.
A brand new playtest but including an experimental new pve-gamemode. It's in a very early stage but we have been working day and night the last five weeks to make this happen.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/2674bc0b9433bac381c470f8e65343d84dc67683.png[/img]

[b]What is our new pve-game mode all about?[/b]
You start with your team ( max 5 players ) in your Stronghold. Your end goal is to collect all four electron tubes to your radio transmitter and be able to send the extraction rescue signal. 

But you will get resistance! 

The Soviet Army will do everything they can to erase all rebels in Scandinavia. They will try to hunt you down and capture your Stronghold.

Between the attack waves your team needs to get out of your comfort zone, discover our brand new map Berget, and find more resources to gain your defensive gear.

But be aware, that some of the areas are heavily guarded by the enemies.

Airdrops are also the key to winning in this gamemode, from them you get better loot and most important, electron tubes. You need four of them to activate the radio transmitter as it is in our pvp game mode - Transmit.

Remember, if you die under an attack wave it's up to your team.[u] If everybody dies it's game over![/u]

This brand-new game mode is in a very early stage, so don't expect a finished pve-experince but you can already expect resistance from our NPCs and a vibe of what is to come in the future.

We have many ideas about what we want to do with the game mode. Like side missions, more types of enemies, and more to explore in our new map Berget.

We are very happy with what we managed to do in this short amount of time, and we can ́t wait to see what you guys think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/104ae3dc51d51f4636f584cdb331e5c0cbafa858.png[/img]

If you don't find anybody to play with you can play the pve-mode alone. But it's gonna be hard to complete alone.

Please give us feedback on what you think.
We have been so busy with the pve-game mode so not many changes are done to Transmit game mode. But we will have some servers live with the game mode Transmit. After Christmas holidays we will focus again on the Transmit gamemode and experience.

Please invite your friends, and spread the word about this game. That will help us a lot!

Something we have learnt after our playtest is that we really need to ensure that players can enjoy the game even if there are less players active on our global servers. Yes we are a new small indie title and it is going to take time for us to grow the active player numbers. So at early access in first half of 2025 we want to be sure that you always can start up Striden and play.

The last weeks after Steam Next Fest we have explored what we can do about a new PVE gamemode in STRIDEN. It started as a prototype but after exploring the possibilities of what we can do in the STRIDEN universe we took a decision to fulfill our vision with a new game mode that you can create your own server and play together with four friends. Yes STRIDEN is going to have a COOP mode! It feels a bit risky to do this so tight into our early access release but it is going to be worth it.

[b]So what is our COOP game mode all about?[/b]
You start with your team in a Stronghold with basic gear to loot inside your base. Your task is to survive enemy attackers ( Soviet Army ) trying to capture your Stronghold. Between the attacking waves you need to explore the map to secure more resources to get better gear. Lootable areas are guarded by enemies and some of them are like a mini mission to complete. The longer you survive the harder the attacking waves are going to be. So building your defence is very important.
To win you need to collect 4 electron tubes to activate your radio transmitter as it is in our PVP gamemode Transmit. BUT if everybody dies it's game over. The only chance to respawn is if any of your team members survive an attacking wave. Kinda hardcore but insanely fun and immersive.

[previewyoutube=jDvU1pV-wjA;full][/previewyoutube]

We will describe more of our new COOP gamemode in a later post. So be sure to join our Discord, wishlist and follow STRIDEN at Steam to stay updated.

We also are going to work hard on all feedback we get from you guys, and keep developing all content that we want to have in place, ready for early access next year!

Our old version had too many triangles and un-optimized assets connected to it so it was a performance issue after some testing.
Now we have re-modeled the house from the ground up with performance as our main goal. We also have built it up now for our future content, for example: later on in the game we want teams to be able to make the Stronghold house a fortress/bunker with pre-placed assets but also the possibility to build it your way with class construction items.

notes.title: Prepare for Playtest! | September 27th
notes.content:
[h3]Hello everybody!
We are now less than one week away from our next open playtest, and we are thrilled to welcome all of you back to the battlefield to fight for survival.
We have been working hard to implement as many updates as possible for this upcoming session. Our primary focus has been on this:[/h3]

[h3][b]Custom settings for the player.[/b][/h3]
FOV slider that many of you have been asking for is now in place.
You can now choose a field of view from 70 to 110. With this change, we had to rewrite our aim-down sight code so that it works with different types of FOV. In our internal tests, this feature has received very positive feedback from the players. Standard FOV has been 80.

Keybinding is something that we have added to. So now you can set your custom inputs in the game settings that fit you best.

Mouse senses got an overlook and it's now easier to set up.

[h3][b]First step to make it easier to play with friends.[/b][/h3]
We also have a first version of joining friends who already are inside a server. You can do that in the Steam overlay like you do in other games. Join a friend or invite a friend to a server. This is something we will keep working on like lobbies and so on in the menu.

[h3][b]Weapons & Gunplay[/b][/h3]
Last official version of the game all weapons had too much bloom in ads. This gave the feeling of a bad hit registration. In this case, this had nothing with the server performance to do. Is about a hard heat bloom for all weapons in ads. To prevent this we have now a new recoil code in the game with different types of recoil patterns. Now it's less bloom and up to the player to master the recoil. We hope that we still maintain the feeling of the weapon that most of you liked. For this pass, all the weapons in the game have been overhauled to feel better and perform greater. ARs are more powerful now and SMG are better at close range.

All weapon sights have been overhauled too. RDS ( red dot sights ) have a new shader on them performing more realistic and a new “dot” texture has been added to them.

All sniper rifle scopes have been reworked. Now they feel better and not as off as before.

Our explosive weapons have been overhauled with changes in the projectile's velocity/gravity, sound effects, and damage fall-off.
   
All the weapons still need tweaks and polish to make them perfect but we hope you feel the difference. We still have a lot of work, one nasty bug is that when you reload the weapon and then aim in the middle of the reload animation the wrong aim offset adds to the weapon. Just aim down sight again and it will be the right aim offset. We are going to fix this, we promise.

Our damage models on the soldiers are now working as it meant to work. We have 3 types of damage zones on the players. Low damage: Arms & Legs. Standard damage: Torso. High Damage: Head.

Nothing groundbreaking but in our last playtest low damage zones didn't work.

We still going to be aware of all feedback around the weaponplay we want it to be great. We are not aiming for a realistic tactical shooter experience. We want something between realistic and arcade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/f68e18c2478181a3e2b34950d1d93917d4d09e6b.gif[/img]


[h3][b]Keep developing content that is missing and new features.[/b][/h3]
Let's talk about the radioactive fog. In the first official version of the game, the fog was kinda meh. Most of it was placeholders but our idea is that the fog will have a bigger impact on the game. The fog is a tempo changer in the match, slowing down the fighting for a while. A perfect time to spend time in your base building up the defense. But if you want to fight outside you need to be prepared.

Last, playtest all you needed to do was press the gas mask key (G) to equip the gas mask, after that, you were safe in the fog. Now we have started to develop a more depth to the fog system. One of them is the gas mask.

Now you need to loot gas mask filters. They will wear out when they are exposed to radioactivity. When you see the status on your gas mask filter is low, change the filter. If you do not have any clean filters in your inventory you are in trouble.

In the world, you can find clean filters and used filters. Now you are thinking, what can I do with used filters? We have a new construction item called the Gas Mask Filter Station that you can build inside your captured Stronghold. In that station, you can clean used filters and use them again. So be sure to loot a lot of filters to be able to fight outside the radioactive fog.

We are also working on radioactive zones on the map. In them, you can find bigger loot stashes and better loot. But these places will drain your filters way faster.

All of this new system is a work in progress but the main goal is that the fog is now a threat for all the soldiers.

But be sure to have filters on you! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/ab1b77bbb9ddc471567b3a2b661bab4fe0da80da.jpg[/img]
 
Our third map Kolarin is ready for testing! Kolarin is right now our biggest map in STRIDEN. It takes place on the Northern Swedish / Finnish border. Populated with a big military airfield, a wood industry area, a small village with a Scandinavian church, and surrounded by big fields with trenches. All Strongholds are in the middle of the map with close distance between them. Our internal testers say this is the best map so far in STRIDEN so we hope that you are going to like it.

We have also added loot boxes to the new map.

But this map needs a lot of testing and work before we can call it done.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/26c6e9b1859e5a40de587353ebe3f71eebfd9a32.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/47ae46e50e7ed5e64ed76035b41d6ebc953b4c39.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/89ef40b96ac6de66d1f3b341f661c287fdcbf92d.png[/img]

We have updated the stamina system. Now it behaves more naturally and with our new sound code for it, it sounds much more realistic. You can hear what state your soldiers are in with and without your gas mask. This gives the game a more immersive feeling to the players.

Fall damage systems have also been reworked to behave better.



[h2]We can't wait to see you all in STRIDEN again. We really believe that we have something new in the FPS genre. It's a hard task to do, but together with you, we can do this together. Invite all your friends and spread the word. That will help us a lot to keep developing this game.[/h2]



[h3]Here is a list of all the changes and new features we have done in the last 1,5 months:[/h3]

sound effect

notes.title: NEW PLAYTEST AROUND THE CORNER
notes.content:
First and foremost, we want to thank everyone who played the early demo of STRIDEN. Thousands of you participated in our playtest week, and it was incredible to see so many of you playing and streaming our upcoming game. We've learned a lot from this experience.

Our most significant oversight was not including an in-game tutorial, and for that, we sincerely apologize. Many players were unsure of what to do, which led to some leaving the game early in the week. However, we were fortunate to have some dedicated FPS players who quickly mastered the game mode and shared their knowledge with others. From now on, we at 5-Fortress will call these players the Heroes of STRIDEN. We deeply appreciate everyone who helped new players understand the game.

Midway through the week, we released a quick "How to Play STRIDEN" video, but we recognize that in-game tutorials would have been more effective. Over the past few weeks, we've been gathering all the feedback from players. While we're still early in the game's development and are aware of many issues, there are specific areas we'll be focusing on:

[list]
[*] Player Settings: Including an FOV slider and custom input customization/keybinding.
[*] Power Spike System (Animals): Balancing, time limits, ease of use, mobility, and force quit.
[*] Gunplay: Many players liked the TTK, so we won't change that, but we will make adjustments. For instance, some weapons had too much bloom/heat, leading players to think there were network/hit registration issues. We plan to reduce bloom overheating and implement recoil patterns to improve aiming accuracy. We'll also be reviewing all AR and LMG weapons, as they currently feel underpowered compared to SMGs.
[*] Ease of Joining Friends: Simplifying the process of joining friends and switching teams during a match.
[*] Game Mode Clarity: Making it easier to understand the game mode and objectives.
[*] Gas and Gas Masks: Adding more depth and complexity.
[*] Fall Damage: Tweaks to improve the experience.
[*] Performance and Optimization: Ensuring smoother gameplay.
[*] Weapon Table Overhaul: Making it easier to manage weapon parts in the stash.
[/list]
We’ll also continue developing new features for the game. As mentioned, we are a small team of six with high ambitions so that progress may take some time.

For daily updates on our progress, please join our Discord channel.

[h3]Now, let's talk about the next playtest session. On September 27th, 2024, we will have a playtest weekend. You'll be able to test the latest developments and see how the game has progressed. We can't wait to play with all of you again, and perhaps you'll explore our third map, Kolarin.

A big thank you to everyone for your support. See you in STRIDEN![/h3]

notes.content:
[h2]A lot of you have requested a tutorial on how to play STRIDEN. Here is a very basic one! [/h2]

[previewyoutube=p4-C7MIkWG4;full][/previewyoutube]


Hey everyone! 
Glad to see so many players trying out our first open playtest session for STRIDEN. Thanks for playing and giving us feedback on how we can improve the game for Early Access. 
Something that we heard a lot is that we missed a tutorial on how to play the game. We are sorry that the game does not include it but we want to give it a shot here. 
So we made a super quick video for the absolute basics of the game functions. Here are some other tips and info that the video does not have. 

Class infos:: 

● Assault: 
		○  Class Ability: Dynamite Stick - Chock explosives that kills enemies in a radius  of 4-5 meters. It also can breach up Enemy Stronghold Doors & Windows.  
		○  Construction Item: Sentry Gun - Guards your Stronghold from enemies. Very  effective against bears. 

● Engineer:  
		○  Class Ability: Breaching tool - Can breach into locked loot places like military storages, bunkers, containers and Strongholds.  
		○  Construction Item: Barricades walls 

● Medic:  
		○  Class Ability: Healing Soup Can - Heal your teammates by holding down the left mouse button or right mouse button to heal yourself.  
		○  Construction Item: Stationary Healing Station 

● Support:  
		○  Class Ability: Ammo box - Restore ammo for you and teammates by throwing it out on the ground.  
		○  Construction Item: Stationary Ammo Crate & Vending Machine where you can store Food and Drinks. Hit it with your hammer eject storage items.  

● Spotter:  
		○  Class Ability: Spawn Beacon: Placeable Spawn point with low respawn time.  
		○  Construction Item: Land mines that you can dig down everywhere on the  landscape.  

Loot tips:  
		●  Military Areas have more weapon parts then other regions  
		●  Industry Areas have more Blueprints but less Weapon Parts  
		●  Civilian infrastructures have more food & drinks items.  

Weapon tips:  
		●  Remember to store your weapons parts into the weapon table. Then you can share weapon parts with your teammates  
		●  You have 3 weapons slots: Primary, Secondary & Explosives.  
		●  Airdrops are the only source of Rare & Epic weapons parts that you need to upgrade weapons. That's why Air Drops are so important in the game.  
		●  Remember that you can upgrade your bought weapon by clicking the variant button. 

Gamemode tips:  
		●  Remember to close the door when you leave the stronghold. When it is closed enemies can not open it, only breach it.  
		●  You can steal electro tubes from enemies' strongholds. They can also steal for you, so have a good defense.  
		●  Airdrops is the best source for team score, if you stand in the inner radius you will get 50 team score every 4 second and other radius 25 team score every 4 seconds.  
		●  The more teammates you are inside the airdrop capture radius the quicker it progresses.  
		●  Use our VOIP System to communicate with your teammates. Hold LEFT ALT.  
		●  Hold Q to use a common rose. Tap Q to spot enemies  
		●  Support have ammo crates, so be sure to have support in your team and also build  an ammo crate inside your Stronghold with your Support Class.  
		●  If you hear a click sound from a land mine, standstill your teammates can diffuse it.  50/50 chance to succeed. Spotter Class have a 100% chance to diffuse it.  
		●  You can respawn on teammates, spawn beacons, strongholds and spawn beacons.  
		●  Best way to kill a bear is with a shotgun ( Secondary weapon in weapon table )  

Also remember that this is a work in progress build of the game, we have more to do before early access. The game still lacks lots of functions, content, balancing, sound mixes and content. So we are so happy that you guys are taking the time to test the game and give us all the feedback that you have. Thank you and see you in STRIDEN.

[h3]We are thrilled to announce that on June 10th, you will finally have the opportunity to play a demo of STRIDEN at Steam Next Fest! After a year of silence, we're back and ready to share our progress with you.

Join us for a week-long event where you can dive into the world of STRIDEN and experience the gameplay firsthand. From now on, we’ll be providing frequent updates on the production and progression of the game.

We can't wait to hear your thoughts and feedback. Get ready to explore, play, and help shape the future of STRIDEN![/h3]

notes.title: Development Recap | Jan 30
notes.content:
[h2]Finally, we can begin sharing and discussing the progress we have made since the beginning of 2022. [/h2]

[h3]Last year presented many exciting opportunities and challenges for our team and studio. We choose to focus on developing a new full-production game, incorporating feedback and influences from our previous project Shattle, while also considering what we could deliver.[/h3]

[h3]For our new game, STRIDEN, we have pushed ourselves to our limits. With more time, innovation, efficiency, and a solid plan, we see the shape of a fun first-person shooter emerging.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43549018/fe750f284fcff774dfd8eec924796b74b943dc4c.png[/img]
Our first map - Vargen

[h3]At the start of 2022, we focused on creating a solid structure for the project using agile management to handle any changes or feedback efficiently. Once this was in place, we immediately began playtesting and shaping the game's core. In the autumn, we implemented more crucial elements to the game loop, and it's becoming clear that our plans are coming to fruition. This was not the case with Shattle, as we had less time and it was a concept game.

In the Development Recap, we will delve deeper into each feature, character, map, and how we brought them to life. Some new systems and innovations have been necessary for us as a small team to deliver the highest quality possible.


We welcome you to STRIDEN and our community! We are eager to hear your thoughts and feedback.[/h3]
